draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Colva! Long before the crowds, Goa's elite came here for their mudanca, a change of air, on what was then the Roiz family's private beach. Today the 2.5 km stretch of sand is part of a 25 km coastline running from Bogmalo to Cabo de Rama.
draft.hungryLine: Head for the beach shacks near Colva resort, there are lots of them.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Walk the beach, then head into the village to see Colva Church and the old elite houses, some with ruins over 300 years old.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Find a spot on the sand for sunset, it's what the weekend crowds come for.
moodReplies.surprise-me: The crown on the statue of Our Lady at Colva Church carries the initials of the Roiz family, who founded the church in 1630.

spots.name: Colva Beach
spots.detail: In Colva · About 2.5 km of sand, best known for its sunsets

spots.name: Colva Church
spots.detail: In Colva · The Church of Our Lady of Mercy, founded in 1630

legends.title: A change of air
legends.body: Goa's aristocratic families used to come to Colva for their mudanca, a change of air by the sea. They stayed near the private beach of the Roiz family.

tips.title: Stay for sunset.
tips.body: On weekends huge crowds gather on the beach just to watch the sun go down.

tips.title: Expect October crowds.
tips.body: The beach gets especially busy in October, when pilgrims come to visit Colva Church.

story.title: The Roiz church
story.body: The Roiz family founded the Igreja de Nossa Senhora das Merces in 1630. Their initials are still on the crown of Our Lady's statue.

story.title: A retreat by the sea
story.body: Colva mattered to the Portuguese and to local noble families. Goa's elite came here for a change of air on the Roiz family's private beach.

story.title: Old houses, big sunsets
story.body: The old quarter mixes elite houses, modern villas and ruins more than 300 years old. Visitors from all over come for the beach and the sunsets.
